stories.title: Sakana adds faster and deeper Marlin research modes
stories.alt: Conceptual comparison of Sakana Marlin modes: Sunlight for general research, Twilight 2.0 for fast broad coverage and Midnight 2.0 for deeper verification; no measured accuracy comparison.
stories.facts: Sakana AI added Twilight 2.0 and Midnight 2.0 to Marlin and redesigned PowerPoint export across all modes. Each new mode consumes 300 credits per investigation versus 100 for Sunlight.
stories.inference: Benchmark source accuracy, coverage, latency and cost on a fixed research task before choosing a deeper mode. More sources do not establish better decisions.
stories.uncertainty: Speed, breadth and verification improvements are vendor claims; no independent accuracy or financial-return validation was verified.

stories.title: News-embedding study exposes a pretraining-memory hazard
stories.alt: Conceptual decomposition of news-embedding predictability into event categories, persistent firm information and possible pretraining memory; no performance figures implied.
stories.facts: The preprint finds that simple event-category forecasts outperform embedding forecasts at short horizons. At longer horizons, earlier firm coverage explains substantial predictability; a calibration shows pretraining memory can reproduce part of the pattern.
stories.inference: Require an event-category baseline and an encoder trained before the evaluation period. Separate genuinely new information from firm identity and historical coverage.
stories.uncertainty: Unreplicated preprint. Memory attribution depends on calibration and cutoff-comparison assumptions; this is not proof that every news model leaks or that a live strategy is profitable.

stories.title: Nasdaq futures lead a rebound into the shortened session
stories.date: Reuters published November 27, 2026, 1:34 a.m. CST; snapshot 1:13 a.m. CST
stories.credit: Reuters, Nov. 27; futures snapshot 1:13 a.m. CST
stories.alt: Common-zero bar chart of Reuters-reported November 27 futures changes at 1:13 a.m. CST: Dow E-mini plus 0.89%, S&P 500 E-mini plus 1.65%, Nasdaq 100 E-mini plus 2.47%; not live ETF returns.
stories.facts: Reuters reported Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 E-mini futures up 0.89%, 1.65% and 2.47%, respectively, at 2:13 a.m. Eastern as investors returned from Thanksgiving.
stories.inference: Treat the growth-led rebound as a gap-risk input. Recheck SPY/QQQ spreads, displayed size and auction imbalances before execution.
stories.uncertainty: An early reported snapshot, not a current executable feed, SPY/QQQ return or evidence that the rebound will persist. Spreads, depth and slippage were not verified.

stories.title: BEA revises third-quarter real GDP growth to 4.3%
stories.credit: BEA Q3 second estimate, released Nov. 25, 2026
stories.alt: Reported-data panel comparing third-quarter real GDP annualized growth of 3.4% in the advance estimate with 4.3% in the second estimate, an upward revision of 0.9 percentage point.
stories.facts: BEA revised third-quarter real GDP growth from 3.4% to 4.3% at a seasonally adjusted annual rate. Investment and consumer spending drove the upward revision; real private domestic final sales grew 5.8%.
stories.inference: Stress duration-sensitive and growth-sensitive signals against stronger demand. Archive the release vintage rather than replacing historical training inputs with revised data.
stories.uncertainty: A November 25 release, not a new release today. Annualized growth is not a year-over-year rate; further revisions are possible and no FOMC action follows mechanically.

stories.title: Black Friday begins with spending forecasts facing inflation pressure
stories.date: Reuters published November 27, 2026, 00:03 UTC (November 26, 6:03 p.m. CST)
stories.credit: Reuters Black Friday preview, Nov. 27 UTC
nodes:
Actual sales totals
Not yet verified
stories.alt: Forecast-versus-results panel showing Reuters-reported holiday-spending growth forecasts of 4% to 6%, inflation pressure and actual Black Friday sales totals not yet verified.
stories.facts: Reuters reports holiday-spending forecasts of 4%–6% growth from last year while consumer sentiment remains shaky and inflation pressures shoppers.
stories.inference: For XRT/XLY research, separate nominal spending, unit demand and promotional margins. Wait for timestamped actual results before treating forecasts as realized demand.
stories.uncertainty: These are forecasts for holiday spending, not observed Black Friday sales growth or inflation-adjusted demand. Full-day sales and retailer margins remain unknown.
